title: Erdős Problem #167: Tuza's Conjecture
description: If G is a graph with at most k edge-disjoint triangles, can G be made triangle-free by removing at most 2k edges? Tuza's Conjecture (1981) remains open in general.

overview.historicalContext:
Tuza conjectured in 1981 that $	au(G) \leq 2
u(G)$, where $	au$ is the minimum number of edges whose removal destroys all triangles, and $
u$ is the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles. The trivial greedy argument gives $	au \leq 3
u$ (take all edges of a maximum packing). Haxell and Kohayakawa (1998) improved this to $	au \leq (3 - 3/23)
u \approx 2.87
u$ using probabilistic and algebraic methods. The fractional version $	au^* \leq 2
u^*$ was proved via LP duality, which shows the factor 2 is 'correct' at the continuous level. The conjecture is known for $K_4$-free graphs (Haxell 1999), planar graphs (Tuza 1994), and graphs of bounded treewidth. Complete graphs $K_4$ and $K_5$ achieve equality $	au = 2
u$, showing the constant 2 cannot be improved.
overview.problemStatement: Let ν(G) be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles in G, and τ(G) the minimum number of edges to remove to make G triangle-free. Tuza's Conjecture: τ(G) ≤ 2·ν(G). K₄ and K₅ show 2 is best possible.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines triangles, edge-disjoint packings, and triangle covers. Aristotle verified three key theorems: (1) trivial_bound: τ ≤ 3ν via constructing a cover from a maximum packing, (2) k4_tight and k5_tight: K₄ and K₅ achieve τ = 2ν exactly, verified by native_decide.
keyInsights: Trivial bound: remove one edge per triangle in maximum packing → τ ≤ 3ν
K₄ achieves equality in Tuza: ν(K₄) = 1, τ(K₄) = 2
K₅ also achieves equality: ν(K₅) = 2, τ(K₅) = 4
Proven for special classes: K₄-free, planar, random graphs

sections.title: Erdős Problem #167: Tuza's Conjecture on Triangle Covering
sections.summary: States Tuza's conjecture: $\tau(G) \leq 2\nu(G)$ where $\tau$ is the minimum triangle edge cover and $\nu$ is the maximum triangle packing. Gives historical context from Tuza (1981) through Haxell-Kohayakawa's 2.87 bound (1998).

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines `IsTriangle G a b c` (three mutually adjacent distinct vertices), `EdgeDisjoint` (triangles sharing no edges), `maxEdgeDisjointTriangles G` ($\nu(G)$ as sSup), `IsTriangleCover G E` (removing $E$ makes $G$ triangle-free), and `triangleCoverNumber G` ($\tau(G)$ as sInf).

sections.title: Tuza's Conjecture
sections.summary: Formalizes `TuzaConjecture`: for all graphs $G$, $\tau(G) \leq 2 \cdot \nu(G)$. Notes this is open in general but proven for special graph classes.

sections.title: Trivial Bound
sections.summary: Proves `trivial_bound`: $\tau(G) \leq 3\nu(G)$ (Aristotle-verified). Strategy: take a maximum packing $T$, collect all edges of triangles in $T$ to form a cover $E$ with $|E| \leq 3|T|$. Maximality of $T$ ensures no triangle survives. Also proves `exists_max_packing` establishing the packing exists.

sections.title: Known Results
sections.summary:
Proves $K_4$ and $K_5$ achieve $	au = 2
u$ exactly (Aristotle-verified via `native_decide`): $K_4$ has $
u = 1, 	au = 2$; $K_5$ has $
u = 2, 	au = 4$. Axiomatizes the Haxell-Kohayakawa bound $	au \leq (3 - 3/23)
u \approx 2.87
u$ and Tuza's conjecture for $K_4$-free and planar graphs.

sections.title: Fractional Version
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the fractional Tuza conjecture $\tau^*(G) \leq 2\nu^*(G)$, which IS proven. The fractional relaxation allows weights in $[0,1]$ and follows from LP duality.

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Recaps: 3 Aristotle-verified theorems (trivial bound, $K_4$ tightness, $K_5$ tightness), 5 axioms (Haxell-Kohayakawa, $K_4$-free case, planar case, fractional version, Tuza conjecture). The gap between the best known 2.87 and the conjectured 2 remains open.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #167 (Tuza's Conjecture) is PARTIALLY SOLVED. This formalization includes three Aristotle-verified theorems: the trivial 3ν bound and tightness examples K₄ and K₅. The conjecture τ ≤ 2ν remains open for general graphs.
conclusion.implications: Tuza's conjecture connects triangle packing (combinatorial optimization) with covering (vertex/edge cover theory). The fractional version being true suggests the integral conjecture may hold with better rounding techniques.
openQuestions: Does τ(G) ≤ 2ν(G) hold for all graphs?
Can the Haxell-Kohayakawa bound 2.87 be improved?
What graph families beyond K₄-free and planar satisfy Tuza?
Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for τ(G) when Tuza holds?

crossReferences.description: Ramsey's theorem guarantees monochromatic cliques; Tuza's conjecture concerns the covering/packing duality for triangles (3-cliques) — both are central to extremal graph theory
Erdős #1079 concerns Turán density in neighborhoods — another extremal problem relating local triangle structure to global graph properties
